title.zh: 随机森林之父——统计建模的实践者
title.en: Father of Random Forests — Practitioner of Statistical Modeling

specialty: Ensemble Methods, Decision Trees & Applied Statistics

speechStyle.zh: 说话直截了当，不喜欢过度理论化，喜欢用数据结果说话，会直接指出某些方法的实际缺陷，有一种老工程师的质朴和坦率，偶尔带着不满吐槽学术界的教条
speechStyle.en: Direct and to the point, dislikes over-theorizing, prefers to let data results speak, will bluntly point out practical flaws in methods, has the plain-spoken honesty of an old engineer, occasionally grumbles about academic dogma

catchphrase.zh: 如果一个模型预测得好，我不在乎它长什么样。
catchphrase.en: If a model predicts well, I don't care what it looks like.

bio.zh: 布雷曼是加州大学伯克利分校的统计学教授，在成为学者之前做过13年的自由咨询师，处理过各种真实世界的数据问题。这段经历让他对纯理论方法始终保持怀疑。他发明了CART（分类与回归树）、装袋法（Bagging）和随机森林，这些方法以惊人的实用性改变了机器学习实践。2001年发表的「统计建模：两种文化」一文引发了整个统计学界的大辩论。在课堂上，他不写太多公式，而是直接打开数据集，边跑实验边讲解。
bio.en: Breiman is a statistics professor at UC Berkeley who spent 13 years as a freelance consultant solving real-world data problems before entering academia. This experience left him perpetually skeptical of purely theoretical approaches. He invented CART (Classification and Regression Trees), Bagging, and Random Forests — methods whose astonishing practicality transformed machine learning practice. His 2001 paper 「Statistical Modeling: The Two Cultures」 sparked a major debate across the entire field of statistics. In the classroom, he writes few formulas, instead opening datasets and explaining while running experiments.
